topicName: Eval and Query for Large Datasets
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Eval and Query for Large Datasets in Pandas"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When working with massive datasets in Pandas, standard vectorized operations create temporary intermediate arrays in memory. The eval and query methods provide a way to evaluate string-based expressions directly, reducing memory overhead and improving performance for large DataFrames."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding DataFrame.eval()"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The eval() method evaluates Python expressions as strings to create or modify columns. It utilizes the numexpr library under the hood when available, allowing for multithreaded evaluation and avoiding the creation of full-sized temporary arrays."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Create a large dataset
n = 1000000
df = pd.DataFrame({
    'a': np.random.rand(n),
    'b': np.random.rand(n),
    'c': np.random.rand(n)
})

# Standard Pandas approach
df['result_standard'] = df['a'] + df['b'] - df['c']

# Eval approach
df.eval('result_eval = a + b - c', inplace=True)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding DataFrame.query()"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"The query() method filters DataFrame rows using a boolean expression string. It is often more readable and memory-efficient than traditional boolean indexing, especially for complex conditions involving multiple columns."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"# Standard boolean indexing
filtered_standard = df[(df['a'] > 0.5) & (df['b'] < 0.5)]

# Query approach
filtered_query = df.query('a > 0.5 and b < 0.5')"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Using External Variables with the @ Symbol"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can reference local Python variables inside your eval and query strings by prefixing them with the '@' symbol. This keeps your expressions dynamic without requiring string concatenation."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"threshold = 0.7

# Using the @ symbol to reference local variables
filtered_threshold = df.query('a > @threshold')"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices and Performance Tips"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Dataset Size: Use eval and query primarily for large DataFrames (typically over 100,000 rows) where memory overhead is a bottleneck."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Engine Selection: Ensure the numexpr package is installed in your environment to unlock C-speed performance and multithreading."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Inplace Operations: Use inplace=True in eval when modifying existing DataFrames to avoid unnecessary object allocation."}]
